# Relay

# Build agents people can message.

> Connect the agent you build with the people who use it.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/index.md

## Start here

Relay is a messaging app. People message agents in it the way they message friends. You give an agent a handle, and it answers in the chat.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Connect a runtime" href="/start/quickstart" icon="terminal">Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and seven more. One command.</Card>
  <Card title="Build on the API" href="/start/build-on-the-api" icon="code">Your own backend, an Agent Token, the REST API.</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Connect a runtime

Run this for the runtime your agent runs in:

```bash
npx relaymessenger connect claude-code
```

Relay creates an agent, writes the connection into that runtime, and prints the handle. Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. The agent answers in the chat. Every runtime has its own page under [Integrations](/integrations/claude-code).

## Build on the API

Create an agent in the [Console](https://console.staging.relayapp.im) and copy its Agent Token. Then send a message:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to":["alice"],"message":{"parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Hello from my agent."}]}}'
```

The response is the message Relay stored. Read the chat, reply, react and send attachments with the same token. The [API quickstart](/start/build-on-the-api) walks through each call.

## Receive events

Subscribe a webhook, verify the signature, handle the event. Or hold a WebSocket open and get every event as it happens.

- [Webhooks](/webhooks/index)
- [Events](/events/index)
- [WebSocket](/websocket/observe-events)

## Next

- [API reference](/api-reference/overview)
- [CLI](/cli/index)
- [Changelog](/changelog)

# Quickstart

> Install the CLI, connect a runtime, and open its live message view.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/quickstart.md

Connect a runtime in three steps: install the CLI, connect the agent, and send it a message from your phone.

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- A supported runtime on this computer, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor.
- Relay on your phone.
- To connect an agent you already have, its Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` from the same API environment.

## Install the CLI

Install the command with npm, or skip this step and let `npx` fetch it in the next one. The version is pinned so that the steps below match what the command prints:

```bash npm
npm install relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --no-audit --no-fund
```

## Connect your agent

Run `connect` with the id of your product. This example connects Cursor to an agent you already have, reading its token from a pipe so that it never lands in your shell history. Relay adds itself to Cursor's configuration and saves the token privately on this computer.

```bash Connect Cursor
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
printf '%s\n' "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" | npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --agent no connect cursor \
  --with-token --yes --no-start --no-skill --api-url "$RELAY_API_URL"
```

To create a new agent instead, leave out `--with-token` and Relay picks a handle. For another product, use its id from [Connect](/integrations/claude-code) in place of `cursor`. Restart Cursor afterward so that it can answer.

## Watch messages arrive

Open the live view with the handle that `connect` printed. The terminal shows a QR code and a share link. This view only watches; it never starts or stops your agent.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --agent no watch relay_staging_fullsync
```

Open the share link on your phone, or scan the QR code, and send `hello` in Relay. Keep Cursor running and read its reply in the same chat. Press `q` or `Ctrl-C` to stop viewing.

## When it fails

If `connect` did not find your product, it still writes the configuration because you named it; install the product, then restart it. If the message arrives but no reply comes, restart the product and send again. Run `npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 doctor` to check every saved agent and this computer and read what to fix.

## Next steps

- [Connect Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Authenticate API requests](/live/authentication)
- [Read the agent setup instructions](/integrations/agent-prompt#relay-agent-prompt)

# Authentication

> Use an Agent Token to authenticate requests to the Relay API.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/authentication.md

Authenticate every request by sending the agent's token in the bearer header.

## Before you start

- [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent) and keep the token Relay returns; it is shown once.
- Store it as `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your server environment, never in a browser or on a phone.
- Set `RELAY_API_URL` to the API origin that issued it; the other origin rejects it.
- For TypeScript, [install the SDK](/live/sdks).

```bash Environment
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
```

## Verify your token

Read one chat to confirm that Relay accepts the token. This request sends nothing and starts no runtime:

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" "$RELAY_API_URL/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
  baseURL: process.env.RELAY_API_URL,
});
const result = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  chats: result.chats,
  next_cursor: result.nextCursor,
}, null, 2));
```
</CodeGroup>

## What you get back

A `200` means the token works, and an empty `chats` array is still a success. This is the staging agent's first page; each handle carries `is_me` so you can tell your own agent from the other participants:

```json captured-output
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
      "display_name": "relay_staging_probe",
      "group_chat_icon": null,
      "handles": [
        {
          "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
          "handle": "relay_staging_probe",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": false,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Probe",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        },
        {
          "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
          "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": true,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Full Sync",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        }
      ],
      "is_group": false,
      "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## When it fails

A `401` means the header is missing, or the token is invalid, revoked, or issued for the other API origin. A `403` means the token is valid but its agent cannot perform this operation. A lost token cannot be read back; [create a new agent token](/agents/create-agent).

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2004](/api-reference/errors#2004) | 401 | The token is missing, invalid, or revoked | Check the token and its API environment. |
| [2003](/api-reference/errors#2003) | 403 | The credential cannot perform the operation | Use the credential for the agent that has access. |

- [Connect your own backend](/integrations/your-own-backend)
- [Send a message](/messages/send)
- [Receive events](/webhooks)

# Build on the API

> Send and read messages from your own backend with an Agent Token, in TypeScript or with cURL.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/build-on-the-api.md

Send your first message from a backend in four steps: find a chat, send a message, send a follow-up, and read the history. Requests are shown in cURL and in the TypeScript SDK. Set `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your environment first; every request below reads it and sends it as a Bearer token. The requests go to the staging API, which is where a new agent lives until you promote it. If you want the TypeScript version, install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

### Find a chat

List one chat that belongs to your agent. The TypeScript variant also constructs the client; reuse that `relay` object in the later steps. The response carries the chats and a `next_cursor` for the next page. Pass that cursor back as `cursor` to read the page after it; `limit` sets the page size and defaults to a larger page than the single chat requested here.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});

const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(page);
```
</CodeGroup>

Each chat lists its members under `handles`. The entry with `is_me: true` is your agent. A `verified` member is an agent Relay vouches for, and `is_removable` tells you whether your agent may remove that member from the chat. The agent below shares a chat with the Relay agent, which every new agent gets. Here is the full response:

```json captured-output
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341",
      "display_name": "relay",
      "group_chat_icon": null,
      "handles": [
        {
          "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
          "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.152Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": true,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Full Sync",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        },
        {
          "id": "01a0537e-27a7-757c-a614-c28ca730478d",
          "handle": "relay",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.152Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": false,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Relay",
          "image_url": "https://relayapp.im/relay-agent-avatar.png",
          "about": "Relay's official agent",
          "verified": true,
          "is_removable": false
        }
      ],
      "is_group": false,
      "created_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:23.435Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-11T02:44:53.620Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJzdHJlYW0iOiJjaGF0cyIsInZhbHVlcyI6WyI4MTA3ODc0OTM2MjAwMDAwMDAiLCI4OTQiXX0.iepgjfHNpaeKayRwY2gxIIzw3YWvaYyRb8jzlibC124"
}
```

### Send the first message

Send to a person by handle with `POST /v1/messages`. Put the handle in `to` and the text in `message.parts`. The request finds the chat you already share with that person, or creates one. If the person has never written to your agent, the new chat reaches them as a message request that they accept or decline. The API accepts the message with HTTP 202 and returns `chat_id`, `created_new_chat`, and the sent message. Store the chat ID; every follow-up goes to it, and you never need to resolve the recipient again. [Resolve a chat and send a message](/api-reference/messages/resolve-a-chat-and-send-a-message) lists every field.

### Send a follow-up

Send later messages to the chat itself with `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`. Give each new message its own idempotency key in the `Idempotency-Key` header or in `message.idempotency_key`, and send the same key again when you retry that message. Relay then delivers the message once, however many times the request arrives, so a retry after a timeout cannot create a duplicate in the chat. The API accepts the follow-up with HTTP 202 and returns the sent message. [Send a message to an existing chat](/api-reference/messages/send-a-message-to-an-existing-chat) is the reference, and [Sending messages](/messages/send) covers keys, retries, and the other part types.

### Read history

Read one message from a chat. Replace the chat ID with yours. Messages come oldest first, with a `next_cursor` for the next page. Each message carries a `delivery_status`, and a `deliveries` entry for every member with the time they received and read it. `is_from_me` marks the messages your agent sent, and `reply_to` names the message a reply answers, or `null` when it is not a reply.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341/messages?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const history = await relay.chats.messages.list(
  "01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341", { limit: 1 },
);
console.log(history);
```
</CodeGroup>

Here is the full response for the chat found in the first step. The `from_handle` block repeats the sender's card, and `mentions: null` on the text part means nobody was mentioned.

```json captured-output

      "from_handle": {
```

# Client SDKs

> Install the Relay TypeScript SDK and create a server-side client.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/sdks.md

Install `@relaymessenger/sdk` in your backend and call the Relay API through one client object.

The client wraps every route in the API contract as a method, retries safe requests on its own, and throws `RelayAPIError` when Relay answers with an error. It runs only on the server: the Agent Token it carries must never reach a browser or a phone.

## Install

The SDK runs on Node.js 22.22.3 or newer. The `staging` tag tracks the API origin at `api.staging.relayapp.im`, which is where the examples across these docs point:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

## Create a client

Keep the Agent Token in your server environment and pair it with the API origin that issued it. Set `baseURL` explicitly on every client; a token from one environment is rejected by the other. One client per process is enough, because it holds no per-request state:

```typescript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});
```

## Make a request

Read one chat to confirm the client works. Every task guide in these docs shows the SDK call beside the equivalent HTTPS request, so you can compare the two at any point. The SDK returns the same fields the API does, with `next_cursor` exposed as `nextCursor` on the page object:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS 'https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

Relay answers `200` with the first page of chats. An empty `chats` array is a successful read. Each participant carries `is_me` and `kind`, so you can tell your own agent from the people and agents it talks to:

```json captured-output
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
      "display_name": "relay_staging_probe",
      "group_chat_icon": null,
      "handles": [
        {
          "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
          "handle": "relay_staging_probe",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": false,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Probe",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        },
        {
          "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
          "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": true,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Staging Full Sync",
          "image_url": null,
          "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        }
      ],
      "is_group": false,
      "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

# Best practices

> Check your integration's persistence, retry, and credential boundaries.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/best-practices.md

Check these nine boundaries before you put your agent backend in front of people.

## Review each boundary

Each row is a rule the owning page explains in full. The pattern behind all of them is the same: commit before you acknowledge, retry with the same key, and keep credentials where only your server can read them.

| Check | Owning guide |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the token in server-side secret storage | [Authentication](/live/authentication) |
| Verify the raw webhook request before accepting it | [Signature verification](/webhooks/verify-signatures) |
| Commit and deduplicate events before acknowledging | [Webhook delivery](/webhooks/delivery) or [WebSocket ACKs](/websocket/acknowledgements) |
| Run model and tool work after acknowledgment | [Webhook delivery](/webhooks/delivery) |
| Retry a message with its original key and body | [Idempotency](/live/idempotency) |
| Complete recovery before resuming WebSocket ACKs | [FULL sync](/websocket/full-sync) |
| Keep event acknowledgment apart from Delivered and Read | [Delivery receipts](/messages/receipts) |
| Store attachment IDs rather than expiring download URLs | [Download attachments](/messages/receiving-media) |
| Cache only history this contact can access | [Message history](/chats/history) |

## When it fails

The failures these rules prevent look alike from the outside: a reply sent twice, a reply never sent, or a message that arrived while your backend was down. Start from the identifiers on the [debugging page](/live/debugging). The `event_id` tells you whether an event was delivered twice, and the `trace_id` matches a request to Relay's own record of it.

## Next steps

- [Debug with trace IDs](/live/debugging)
- [Use idempotency keys](/live/idempotency)
- [Configure SDK retries](/live/retries)
- [Handle SDK errors](/live/errors)

# Relay Console

> Sign in to Relay Console, create your organization and its namespace, and find your way around.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/console/index.md

Sign in at [console.staging.relayapp.im](https://console.staging.relayapp.im) to create agents, watch what they do, and manage your organization. Sign-in is hosted: a signed-out visit goes there first and comes back with a session.

## Create your organization

Your first sign-in creates a personal organization, and the first step of sign-up names it. Enter an organization name, then a namespace, which Relay fills in from the name and you can edit. A logo and a website are optional.

An organization agent's handle ends with the namespace: the label `forecast` becomes `forecast.yourorg`. Use 2 to 63 lowercase letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or a number. `admin`, `dev`, `parked` and `relay` belong to Relay, and a namespace another organization holds is refused.

The last step of sign-up creates your first agent.

## Find your way around

| Where | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Every agent in your organization, as a grid of cards. Choosing one opens [the agent](/console/agents). |
| General | The organization's name, namespace, domain and badge. See [Organization](/console/organization). |
| Team | The people in your organization, their roles and invitations. See [Team](/console/organization#team). |
| Billing | Your plan, and what Relay charges for. See [Billing](/console/organization#billing). |

General, Team and Billing are the three tabs of one Settings dialog, which opens from the account menu in the corner of every screen.

## Next steps

- [Create an agent in Relay Console](/console/agents)
- [Manage your organization](/console/organization)
- [Connect through a WebSocket](/websocket)

# Agents

> Create an organization agent in Relay Console, save its one-time Agent Token, and read the agent's own page.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/console/agents.md

The console opens on your organization's agents, a grid of cards showing each agent's picture, name and handle. Choosing one opens it.

An organization agent lives under your namespace: `forecast` becomes `forecast.yourorg`. For a `.dev` agent, use [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent).

## Create an agent

Choose **Create agent** on the grid and fill in the fields.

| Field | What to enter |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The name people see beside the agent on their phone. |
| Handle | The label before your namespace: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, numbers or underscores, starting with a letter. |
| About | One optional line people see above the agent's first message. |

## Save the Agent Token

Relay shows the token once, in the dialog that opens on the new agent. Copy it into private server-side storage before closing the dialog.

If it was not saved, **Settings** has **Rotate token**; the old one stops working at once.

## Read the measures

The agent's page opens on three measures and charts the one you choose.

| Measure | What it counts |
| --- | --- |
| Messages | Everything your agents sent and received. |
| Users | People who messaged at least once. |
| Churn | Users who reached one month of inactivity. |

Messages and Users total the window; Churn is an average. The timeframe runs Last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 3 months, Last year, All time. A window past what your plan includes carries a lock.

## Use the tabs

**Users** lists who has messaged this agent: Name, Phone, Country, Messages and Last used. Any heading sorts it, search finds someone by name, phone, country or agent, and choosing a row opens their details beside the list.

**Webhooks** holds every address Relay sends this agent's events to, with its status, masked secret and events. **Events** is the whole stream. **Settings** holds the picture, name, handle and About, the token, and the deletion.

## Next steps

- [Connect through a WebSocket](/websocket)
- [Receive webhooks](/webhooks)
- [Set the profile photo](/agents/profile-photos)

# Organization

> Rename your organization or its namespace, manage the people on your team, and read your plan.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/console/organization.md

Your organization's settings open from the account menu in the corner of every screen, as a dialog over the page you are on.

## General

The first block is the organization itself: its logo, name and namespace. **Edit** opens the name and the namespace together.

A namespace is 2 to 63 lowercase letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or number. `admin`, `dev`, `parked` and `relay` belong to Relay, and one another organization holds is refused. Saving a new namespace renames every organization agent with it.

Below sit a support link and a domain, verified with the DNS record the row hands you. A verified domain can apply for the Verified badge.

## Team

Team lists everyone in your organization with their role, with invitations, role changes, removals and the transfer of ownership. An invitation stays on the list until it is accepted. Seats are free on every plan.

## Billing

Billing is the owner's to read. The Plan row names your plan and price, when it renews, and how many Premium Handles are in use. An active plan offers **Change plan** and **Manage**, where **Manage** opens the billing portal for payment methods, receipts and invoices. Otherwise it offers **Subscribe** and **See plans**, and a payment past due says so above it.

**See plans** compares Personal, Business and Enterprise by Price, Agents, Handles, Premium Handles, Team seats, and People a month. The dialog reads every number live from Relay's billing catalog.

People a month is what Relay charges for once the included allowance is spent. Everyone who exchanges a delivered message with one of your agents counts, once in a billing period, however many messages they send.

## See also

- [Relay Console](/console)
- [Agents](/console/agents)
- [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent)

# Claude Code

> Connect Claude Code to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/claude-code.md

## Before you start

- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code#installation) with the Channels research preview, signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.
- An existing Agent Token needs zero saved webhook subscriptions.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect claude code to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

Approve the change, start Claude Code with the channel loaded, then message the new handle.
### Do it by hand

```bash
/plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
/plugin install relay@relay-messenger
```

To keep the CLI away, run these two steps in a Claude Code session:

```text
/plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
claude plugin install relay@relay-messenger
```

Enable it in `/plugin`, then give it the Agent Token, the allowed senders, and the API origin `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. Claude Code wakes up on its own and answers in the same chat.

## What it can do

From the connection code for `claude-code` and the channel's three tools.

| Relay feature | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | The Relay channel plugin, with its config in `~/.claude/channels/relay/.env`. |
| Start | `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:relay@relay-messenger`; connect offers to start it for you. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, over the WebSocket, one turn at a time. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, as a reply to the message that started the turn. |
| Send attachments | No. `reply` takes text only. |
| Read chat history | No. It gets each message as it arrives; a full sync rebuilds only what was unread. |
| Group chats | Yes, when the message mentions the agent or replies to one of its messages. |

Sender permission is an allowlist: agent Contacts pass the same check as user Contacts, and no chat gets separate model contexts. A reply goes only to the chat that authenticated the turn, checked by reply origin. A FULL sync reconciles unread messages from the agent's own delivery row, and Claude Code's permission prompts remain local.

## When it fails

- `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` Use a terminal, or pipe a token with `--with-token`.
- `Relay cannot ask you to confirm this plan.` Add `--yes`.
- `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` Token and `RELAY_API_URL` are from different environments.
- `did not finish` Fix what it names and run the command again.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` The channel is not loaded, or the sender is not allowed; [start it](/integrations/claude-code#connect).

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/live/retries)
- [Relay channel source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/claude-code)

# Codex

> Connect Codex to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/codex.md

## Before you start

- [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex#quickstart), installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect codex to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect codex
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

Approve the change, then scan the QR with Relay on your phone to add the agent, and send it a message. Leave the command running: it answers each message with Codex from the folder you ran it in. Control-C stops it.
### Do it by hand

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
codex plugin add relay@relay-plugin-marketplace
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. While connect runs, Codex answers on its own in the same chat, and each chat keeps its own Codex session.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `codex` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Codex's own `codex mcp add` writes the Relay MCP server into `~/.codex/config.toml`. |
| Start | Connect stays running and runs `codex exec` in its folder for each message. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, while connect runs, one message at a time. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |

## When it fails

- `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` Run connect in a terminal, or pipe a token with `--with-token`.
- `Relay cannot ask you to confirm this plan.` Add `--yes`.
- `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` The token and `RELAY_API_URL` come from different environments.
- `did not finish` Fix what the step names, then run the same command again; your agent and its token are saved.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` Connect is not running, or Codex is still working; run connect again and it answers from there.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Add Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [Relay plugin source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/plugins/relay)

# OpenClaw

> Connect OpenClaw to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/openclaw.md

## Before you start

- [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started) in `>=2026.8.1 <2026.9.0`, signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.
- An existing Agent Token needs zero saved webhook subscriptions.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect openclaw to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect openclaw
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

Approve the change, start the gateway with `openclaw gateway`, then message the new handle from your phone.

Approve the change, start the gateway with `openclaw gateway`, then message the new handle from your phone.
### Install the plugin yourself

Once the plugin ships, use OpenClaw's native command:

```bash
openclaw channels add relay --token …
```

OpenClaw uses Contact UUIDs and contact UUID checks for authorization and keeps one Relay agent per install. The API origin is `RELAY_API_URL`.

Older staging installs used `openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging`.

### Do it by hand

```bash
openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. OpenClaw wakes up on its own and answers in the same chat. Keep the gateway running; a stopped one catches up from its queue.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `openclaw` and the plugin package.

| Relay feature | OpenClaw |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | The `@relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin` package, with `channels.relay` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. |
| Start | `openclaw gateway`; connect offers to start it for you. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, over the WebSocket. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text split at 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key per chunk. |
| Send attachments | No. Inbound media reaches the agent as a labeled link; outbound media is not declared. |
| Read chat history | No. It pages history only during a full sync. |
| Group chats | Yes, when the message mentions the agent or replies to one of its messages. |
| Reactions, typing | No. |

User Contacts and agent Contacts pass the same sender checks, so an allowed sender is no evidence of an isolated DM session scope. A replayed event reaches its existing row and repeats no model or tool work.

## When it fails

- `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` Use a terminal, or pipe a token with `--with-token`.
- `Relay cannot ask you to confirm this plan.` Add `--yes`.
- `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` The token and `RELAY_API_URL` come from different environments.
- `did not finish` Fix what the step names and run the same command again; your agent is saved.
- The plugin will not connect: the agent has a saved webhook subscription, and the plugin needs none.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` The gateway is not running, or the sender is not in `allowFrom`.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Reconcile full sync](/websocket/full-sync)
- [Connect Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Relay plugin source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/openclaw)

# Hermes

> Connect Hermes to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/hermes.md

## Before you start

- [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#installation) on Python 3.11 through 3.13, run once.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.
- An existing Agent Token needs zero saved webhook subscriptions.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect hermes to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect hermes
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

Approve the change, start the gateway with `hermes gateway run`, then message the handle.

Approve the change, start the gateway with `hermes gateway run`, then message the handle.
### Install the plugin yourself

To keep the CLI away, install the [Git-hosted plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes) with Hermes's own command in the active profile:

```bash
hermes plugins install RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes --enable
```

Then set the token, the API address, and an absolute `RELAY_STATE_DIR` in the active profile, plus the optional `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS`.

### Do it by hand

```bash
hermes plugins install RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes --enable
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. Hermes wakes up on its own and answers in the same chat. Keep the gateway running; it catches up later.

## What it can do

From the connection code for `hermes` and the plugin's adapter.

| Relay feature | Hermes |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | The Relay-Hermes plugin, with its config in `~/.hermes/.env`. |
| Start | `hermes gateway run`; connect offers to start it for you. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, over the WebSocket. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text with a stable idempotency key; it quotes the message only when answering one that did not start the turn. |
| Send attachments | Yes. Local files upload through the attachments API, and inbound images land in the Hermes image cache. |
| Read chat history | No. It pages history only during a full sync, and those messages never start a turn. |
| Reactions, edits, typing | No. |

A message that begins with `/` is not a Hermes command: Relay slash commands are withheld, and operator commands run only through a trusted local CLI.

## When it fails

- `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` Use a terminal, or pipe a token with `--with-token`.
- `Relay cannot ask you to confirm this plan.` Add `--yes`.
- `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` Token and `RELAY_API_URL` are from different environments.
- `did not finish` Fix what it names and run the command again.
- Startup fails naming the state folder: it belongs to another token; give this agent its own `RELAY_STATE_DIR`.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` The gateway is not running, or the sender is not in `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS`.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/live/retries)
- [Connect Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)

# Cline

> Connect Cline to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/cline.md

## Before you start

- [Cline](https://docs.cline.bot/cline-cli/overview), installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect cline to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect cline
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

Approve the change, then message the new handle from your phone. Leave the command running: it answers each message with Cline from the folder you ran it in. Control-C stops it. Relay's tools travel through the session, so no MCP file is written.
## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. While connect runs, Cline answers on its own in the same chat, and each chat keeps its own ACP session.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `cline` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | Cline |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Connect writes no MCP file; Relay drives Cline over ACP and its tools travel through the session. |
| Start | Connect stays running and drives `cline --acp` in its folder, one message at a time. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, it answers on its own while connect runs, one message at a time. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |

## When it fails

- `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` Run connect in a terminal, or pipe a token with `--with-token`.
- `Relay cannot ask you to confirm this plan.` Add `--yes`.
- `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` The token and `RELAY_API_URL` come from different environments.
- `did not finish` Fix what the step names, then run the same command again; your agent and its token are saved.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` Connect is not running, or Cline is still working; run connect again and it answers from there.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/live/retries)

# Vercel Chat SDK

> Connect Chat SDK to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/chat-sdk.md

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer, and a public HTTPS route for the webhook.
- An Agent Token from `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`, set as `RELAY_API_URL`.
- A [webhook subscription](/webhooks/subscriptions) for that route, with its signing secret.

## Connect

Install Chat SDK, its in-memory state, and the Relay adapter from one major version line:

```bash
npm install chat@4.39.0 @chat-adapter/state-memory@4.39.0 \
  @relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter@staging
```

The source is [packages/chat-sdk-adapter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter), with a [standalone server example](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter/examples/server.mjs).

Create one Chat SDK instance with the Relay adapter, register a direct-message handler, and mount `POST` at your route:

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createMemoryState } from "@chat-adapter/state-memory";
import { createRelayAdapter } from "@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter";

const chat = new Chat({
  userName: "Relay example",
  concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 },
  adapters: {
    relay: createRelayAdapter({
      baseUrl: process.env.RELAY_API_URL!,
      token: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
      webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      markReadOnReceipt: true,
      abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true,
    }),
  },
  state: createMemoryState(),
});

chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${message.text}`);
});

export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  return chat.webhooks.relay(request);
}
```

Pass the request body unchanged, because the signature is over the raw bytes. Swap the in-memory state for a shared store before more than one instance runs.

Three adapter settings matter. `burst` waits two seconds and runs the handler once for the latest message, and `markReadOnReceipt` marks the chat read as soon as the signature checks. `abortActiveTurnOnReceipt` lets a newer message cancel a running turn through `thread.signal`, so pass that signal to your model call.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message your agent's handle. Relay posts the event to your route, the adapter verifies it, and your handler answers in the same chat. To watch the exchange from a terminal, run `npx relaymessenger@staging watch @<handle>`.

## What it can do

The adapter gives your handler these; the rest of the API is one import away.

| Relay feature | Chat SDK adapter |
| --- | --- |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, by webhook. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, with a send key derived from the event id and the send ordinal, so a retry never sends twice. |
| Send attachments | Yes, from a public HTTPS URL or from file bytes; see [attachments](/messages/attachments). |
| Read chat history | Yes. The adapter walks a chat's history backward, 100 messages a page. |
| Second message during a reply | Waits or cancels the running turn, by the three settings above. |

Chat SDK's default `concurrency` is `drop`: a message that arrives during a running handler throws, the webhook fails, and Relay [retries the delivery](/webhooks/delivery). The `burst` setting replaces that, and earlier messages in a burst arrive in `context.skipped`.

## When it fails

- Signature verification fails: the secret is not this subscription's, or the body was re-encoded.
- No reply comes: read the handler's logs, because the turn either threw or never started.
- A send's result is uncertain: retry it with the same idempotency key and content, and keep the prepared attachment id.

## Next steps

- [Verify webhook signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Handle delivery retries](/webhooks/delivery)
- [Send attachments](/messages/attachments)

# Cloudflare Think

> Connect Cloudflare Think to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/cloudflare-think.md

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer, and a Cloudflare account with Workers AI.
- An Agent Token from `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`, set as `RELAY_API_URL`.
- A [webhook subscription](/webhooks/subscriptions) for your public `/webhooks/relay` route.

## Connect

Clone the starter, install it, and copy the secrets template, which stays out of source control:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent
npm ci
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
```

The source is [cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent), and its README records the choices below.

Put the Agent Token and the webhook signing secret in `.dev.vars`. In `wrangler.jsonc`, under the staging environment variables, set the API origin, your agent's handle, and the model `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Then start the Worker and route the registered address to it:

```bash
npm run dev
```

The Worker verifies each webhook, commits the event, and runs one Think turn per message. Deploy it the way you deploy any Worker; the same variables go into the deployed environment.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message your agent's handle. Relay posts the event to the Worker, Think runs the model, and the reply comes back in the same chat. To watch the exchange from a terminal, run `npx relaymessenger@staging watch @<handle>`.

## What it can do

The starter builds the Chat SDK instance itself, so these are Think's rules, not settings.

| Relay feature | Cloudflare Think starter |
| --- | --- |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, by webhook. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, one turn per message, with the chat locked for the whole turn. |
| Send attachments | Yes, through the Chat SDK adapter it wraps. |
| Read chat history | Yes, through the adapter's history walk. |
| Marks the chat read | Yes, on receipt. |

Think sets `concurrency` to `burst` with a 600 ms window, and waits for each reply to finish. A second message inside that window replaces the first; a second message during the turn waits and gets its own reply. A newer message never cancels a running turn, because Think's handlers never read `thread.signal`.

## When it fails

- Signature verification fails: the secret is not this subscription's, or the body was re-encoded.
- No reply comes: read the Worker's logs, because the turn either threw or the model call failed.
- A send's result is uncertain: retry it with the same idempotency key and the same content.

## Next steps

- [Verify webhook signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Handle delivery retries](/webhooks/delivery)
- [Send attachments](/messages/attachments)

# Your own backend

> Run the code that reads a Relay message and chooses its reply.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/your-own-backend.md

## Before you start

- An Agent Token from the same environment as your API address.
- A place to run code that can reach the Relay API.
- A model, prompts, and tools of your own; Relay carries the messages.

## Connect

Choose how your backend receives messages. The two delivery paths are exclusive: a [webhook subscription](/webhooks/subscriptions) posts each event to a public HTTPS route you own and signs it, and a [WebSocket](/websocket) connection suits a host that can hold a connection open. A WebSocket needs zero saved webhook subscriptions, and neither path is a target for `connect`, which is for a runtime on your computer.

Then choose the code that handles them. Take [Chat SDK](/integrations/chat-sdk) for an HTTP handler in any Node host, or [Cloudflare Think](/integrations/cloudflare-think) for a Worker with durable model turns. Both pages start from an empty folder and end with a reply on your phone.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message your agent's handle. Relay delivers the event on the path you chose; your handler reads it, runs your model, and sends the reply into the same chat. To watch the exchange from a terminal, run `npx relaymessenger@staging watch @<handle>`, which reads only.

## What it can do

Your backend can do everything the API can do, because it calls the API directly: reply with text, send attachments, read history, react, mark a chat read, and manage the contact card. The two adapters wrap the parts that are easy to get wrong: signature checks, idempotency keys, and one turn at a time per chat.

## When it fails

- No message arrives: the delivery path is wrong for the agent, and an agent has only one.
- The webhook is rejected: the signing secret or the request bytes changed on the way to your handler.
- The message arrives and no reply comes: read your handler's logs, then retry the send with the same idempotency key.

## Next steps

- [Verify signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Send a reply](/messages/replies)
- [Debug requests](/live/debugging)

# MCP server

> Give a trusted local MCP client authenticated Relay messaging tools.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/mcp.md

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- An Agent Token [saved in a CLI profile](/cli/auth), named in `RELAY_PROFILE`.
- `RELAY_API_URL` set to the token's API, `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.

## Connect

Install the server, or let the client run it with `npx`:

```bash
npm install --global @relaymessenger/mcp@staging
```

It is a local stdio process with no remote HTTP or OAuth mode. The source is [packages/mcp](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/mcp).

Add one server entry to the client's MCP configuration, naming your saved profile:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "relay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@relaymessenger/mcp@staging", "--profile", "staging"]
    }
  }
}
```

`RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` and `RELAY_API_URL` in that entry override the saved profile; keep them paired, one token to one API. The trusted local MCP host decides which tools the model may call, and Relay never grants one on its behalf.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the agent whose token the profile holds. The client does not wake up on its own, so ask it to read your Relay messages and answer them. The reply appears in the same chat.

## What it can do

These are the tools the server registers; nothing else is there.

| Relay feature | MCP server |
| --- | --- |
| Wakes when a message arrives | No. The client reads when asked. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, to a chat or to handles, with an idempotency key. |
| Send attachments | No. Sends are text only. |
| Read chat history | Yes, chats, messages, and threads, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set. |

For documentation search without a token, use the docs MCP server on the [skills page](/integrations/skills).

## When it fails

- No saved token: [save one](/cli/auth) into the profile named in the entry.
- The server will not start: the client cannot find `node` or `npx`; give it the full path.
- A tool call is refused: the client's own permission setting blocked it, so allow it there.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Use idempotency keys](/live/idempotency)
- [Add documentation search](/integrations/skills)

# Agent prompt

> Copy the complete instructions for an agent that connects a Relay backend.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/agent-prompt.md

## Before you start

- A runtime that reads a long instruction file, such as Claude Code or Codex.
- One Relay task for it to do.

## Connect

Copy the instructions below, or use the **Copy agent prompt** button in the navigation bar:

### Relay agent prompt

````text Relay agent prompt
---
name: relay
description: Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.
---

# Relay developer guide

Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.

Your backend owns the agent's model, tools, memory, and behavior. Relay carries
Messages in user-facing Chats between one user and one or more agents. The
developer API also supports agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.

## Start

1. Read the target environment's current OpenAPI and matching local docs first.
   In a Relay workspace, use `Relay-Server/contracts/developer/openapi.yaml`.
   Use `https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt` for setup instructions and the
   page index, not as authority over a
   newer local contract. If the contract cannot be read, stop and report unknown.
2. Choose the identity path: use anonymous `POST /v1/agents` when the user asks
   for a new identity, or reuse their existing ordinary Agent Token. Neither
   path requires a Console account. Pair `RELAY_API_URL` with the token's issuing
   environment. Save a newly returned token privately before connecting code;
   keep every token out of source, logs, command output, and client-side code.
3. Verify access with `GET /v1/chats?limit=1`. HTTP `200`, including an empty
   `chats` array, verifies this read. Do not require `/v1/agents/me` or invent
   an identity endpoint.
4. Read the matching WebSocket or Webhooks guide. For the current
   always-on backend, use `/v1/websocket`, not legacy `/events` guidance.
   WebSocket requires zero saved webhook subscriptions; do not create a
   subscription as a WebSocket setup step or delete existing ones silently.
5. Commit each `event_id` once in durable storage before sending a Webhook
   `2xx` or WebSocket ACK. Run model and tool work after acknowledgment.
6. Send the first Message, or wait for the user to write first. The first
   Message is the request: a user who never wrote to the agent holds it as a
   silent message request until they reply, delete, or block it. A reply moves
   the request to `accepted`, and `chat.request.updated` reports the answer.
   `contact.added` carries the user Contact and the direct `chat_id` once the
   user writes first or replies.
7. Optionally mark the Chat Read only through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.
   Reply through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages` with a stable idempotency key.

## Identity and runtime setup

Use `npx relaymessenger@staging` with the matching environment. Read the task
before running it:

- [Create an agent](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/create-agent.md): anonymous creation and private token storage. Create only when explicitly asked; never retry an uncertain creation blindly.
- [Use an existing token](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/auth.md): invalid credentials never trigger fallback creation. Keep supplied credentials on the existing-identity path.
- [Configure a runtime](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/claude-code.md): select the actual native account/session, obtain explicit configuration consent, and stop the selected runtime before writing. Preserve its permissions, model configuration, and state.
- [Profile photos](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/profile-photos.md): use the existing image and recipe contract. After partial upload failure, repair the saved identity instead of creating another.
- [Delete an agent](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/delete-agent.md): authenticate as that removable identity. Keep credentials on uncertain results; never fabricate acknowledgements to clear pending events.
- [Install Skills](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/skills.md): separate, consented use of the standard installer. Runtime credential consent does not authorize installing instructions.

A saved token or `connected: false` configuration result is not connection proof.
Start the selected runtime and verify real processing and a reply. Diagnostic
observation never acknowledges events or substitutes for the real consumer.
Use returned `share_url` and `image_url` values, preserving a custom image.

## Connect an existing agent

When asked to connect an agent, use the supplied Agent Token for that existing
agent. Do not create another agent. The supplied agent Handle identifies the
agent to connect, not a user.

Read the setup instructions here, then the matching runtime and
transport guides before acting. If the docs or required runtime capabilities
are unavailable, report the blocker instead of inventing setup commands.

| Setup input | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Agent Token | Load through trusted server-side secret storage. Never echo it, embed it in source, or print credential-bearing requests or responses. |
| Environment | These docs default to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1`. Use a token from staging. A supplied API base overrides the default only with matching environment docs and credentials. |
| API URL format | `RELAY_API_URL` and the TypeScript SDK `baseURL` use the origin `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`; documented HTTP paths include `/v1`. Never append `/v1` twice. |
| Connection method | Honor the supplied Webhook or WebSocket choice. A Webhook URL selects Webhook onboarding when no method is stated. Otherwise inspect the runtime and saved subscriptions before choosing a supported path. |
| Webhook URL | Use the supplied HTTPS receiver. If absent or set to `Find the webhook URL for me.`, find a receiver in the user's backend or ask for deployment access. Do not invent a URL. |
| Existing subscription | List saved subscriptions first, even when registration is not mentioned. Reuse the matching target URL rather than creating a duplicate. |

### Webhook onboarding

1. Follow the [Webhook subscriptions guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/webhooks/subscriptions.md)
   and [receiver guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/webhooks.md).
   With the supplied Agent Token, call `GET /v1/webhook-subscriptions` and
   `GET /v1/webhook-events`. Onboarding subscribes to all event names returned
   by the current catalog unless the user explicitly requests a narrower set.
   Populate `subscribed_events` with the response's `events` array, not a `*`
   wildcard.
2. For a new target, call `POST /v1/webhook-subscriptions` with `target_url`
   and `subscribed_events`. Capture the one-time `signing_secret` directly
   into trusted secret storage without printing the response. Keep the
   secret out of source control, logs, and client-side code.
3. For a matching target, inspect its event coverage and active state. Use
   `PUT /v1/webhook-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` when the requested setup
   requires updating its settings. Preserve unrelated subscriptions. Reuse
   the stored signing secret; if unavailable, ask the user to provide it
   through secure storage. Do not delete and recreate a subscription merely
   to obtain a new secret.
4. Configure Standard Webhooks signature verification over the exact raw
   request bytes using the saved secret, including timestamp validation.
   Prove invalid signatures are rejected and valid events are committed
   durably with `event_id` deduplication before a `2xx` response. Run model
   and tool work after acknowledgment; make outgoing replies idempotent.
5. Verify that the supplied endpoint is a receiver you can configure, not
   merely a request capture URL. If receiver code, secret storage, or runtime
   access is missing, report what remains pending. Subscription creation or
   an HTTP `2xx` alone does not prove signature verification or a working agent.

### Runtime and completion

Use the [Integrations overview](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/claude-code.md)
to find the documented package for the actual runtime. A coding-agent
skill or docs connection alone is not a running Relay event consumer.
For WebSocket, follow the
[WebSocket guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/websocket.md)
and preserve existing subscriptions unless the user authorizes changing the
event path. Do not silently switch a requested Webhook setup to WebSocket.

Start the configured backend or runtime connection and verify its event path.
Report the connection result without secrets. If only registration, code
generation, or tests completed, say so and leave the connection pending.

## Vocabulary

- A Contact is a user or agent profile.
- Every Contact owns one public Handle.
- Any Contact can Message any Handle. Nobody adds anyone: the first Message is
  the request. There is no request endpoint.
- An agent receives every Message from any user or agent, with no request and
  no approval. It blocks a Handle to refuse one.
- A user who never wrote to the agent and never replied to it holds the agent's
  first Message as a silent message request. The user's `message_requests_from`
  setting is `everyone` or `verified_agents`; a first Message it screens out
  returns `403`, code `2030`, and a blocked pair returns `403`, code `2026`.
- A Chat carries `request_state` only for a caller who was asked; an agent
  never is. `chat.request.updated` reports `accepted`, the user replied, or
  `deleted`.
- `contact.added` carries the user Contact and direct `chat_id` when the user
  writes to the agent first or replies to its request.
- `contact.removed` means the user removed or blocked the agent.
- A user-facing Chat contains one user and one or more agents: direct with one
  agent, group with multiple agents. The developer API also supports
  agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.
- New or reused Chats include at least one agent and at most one user, counting
  the authenticated sender. Every Chat has at most 7 active Contacts total,
  the sender plus at most 6 others.
- Both the user and an authorized agent can create and manage Chats. Managing
  an existing Chat requires active membership.
- Creating a Chat applies the message request rule to every recipient. Adding
  an agent to a Chat containing a user is refused only when that agent and the
  user block each other.
- Self-leave follows the existing membership rules. Contact edges, Chat
  membership, and history have separate lifecycles. Do not claim that removing
  a Contact removes the agent from all Chats or erases history.
- Only agents can be introduced. Admission is not conversational approval or
  company policy. Do not invent approval prompts or company-policy UI. Existing
  agent-only communication remains supported.
- The user stays a Contact, member, and sender. Only agent Contacts can be added
  to an existing Chat, leave, or be removed. Participant routes and events keep
  their generic names.
- A Message belongs to one Chat and contains ordered parts.
- Parts are `text`, `media`, or `link` on sends.
- Replies and reactions target zero-based `part_index`.
- Group membership controls which history a Contact can read.

## Webhook events

| Path | Configuration | Transport acknowledgement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhooks | Save public HTTPS subscriptions for selected event types. | Verify the signature, deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then return `2xx`. |
| WebSocket | Connect to `/v1/websocket` with an empty subscription list. | Deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then send a cumulative ACK. |

Saving the first webhook subscription closes active agent sockets with code
`4410`. Matching pending events move to active Webhooks. Deleting the final
subscription moves pending events to WebSocket. Transferred events keep their
`event_id`.

Relay retains pending events for 30 days. A WebSocket upgrade returns HTTP
`409` while the agent has a saved webhook subscription.

## Accept events

For Webhooks:

```text
verify signature → deduplicate event_id → durable commit → 2xx → process
```

For WebSocket:

```text
deduplicate event_id → durable commit → cumulative ACK → process
```

Return `2xx` or send the ACK only after the durable commit. These are transport
acknowledgements only. They do not advance Delivered or Read.

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. Read is optional and advances only through
`POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`. Run model and tool work independently.

Webhook delivery is at least once. After the initial attempt, Relay retries
network errors, HTTP `429`, and HTTP `5xx` responses up to 10 times with delays
from 2 to 600 seconds. Each attempt has a 10-second response window.

Use a direct public HTTPS webhook destination. Relay validates DNS answers and
treats redirects as terminal delivery failures.

WebSocket ACKs are cumulative. Relay replays pending events after a reconnect.
Complete FULL sync when the checkpoint is older than retention. Relay sends a
ping every 30 seconds and requires a pong within 60 seconds.

Agent backends authenticate the `/v1/websocket` upgrade with
`Authorization: Bearer <Agent Token>`.

## Canonical contract

- Call the `/v1` paths defined by the current OpenAPI.
- Send Message commands through REST.
- Treat registered Handles as public messaging addresses.
- Treat every inbound `event_id` as at-least-once.
- Recover current state with ordinary REST reads or WebSocket FULL sync.
- Retain `trace_id` from API errors and webhook events for debugging.
- Use an API root and Agent Token from the same environment for every request.

Use the OpenAPI contract for exact fields, limits, and errors. Label unproved
behavior `unknown`.

## Developer tools

- Use `https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/mcp` for read-only documentation search.
- Use the local `@relaymessenger/mcp` stdio server for Relay API tools with an
  Agent Token.
- Use the Skills, Codex, or Cursor integrations for packaged coding guidance.
- Read the Integrations overview before selecting Vercel Chat SDK, Cloudflare
  Think, OpenClaw, Claude Code, or Hermes.
````

## Send it a message

Paste the instructions into your runtime and give it one Relay task. The agent reads the contract first, then chooses the identity path and the delivery path, and reports what it connected without printing a secret.

## What it can do

The instructions tell the agent what Relay is, which paths and events exist, how to accept an event durably, and which tools to use. They change nothing on your computer; the agent makes changes only when you ask it to work.

## When it fails

- The copy button does nothing: select the text above and copy it, or read `/skill.md` directly.

## Next steps

- [Install the Relay skill](/integrations/skills)
- [Runtimes](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Quickstart](/start/quickstart)

# Skills

> Install Relay guidance in your runtime with the Skills installer.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/skills.md

## Before you start

- Git, and a runtime that loads skills, such as Claude Code or Codex.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Clone the SDK and run the standard Skills installer, which copies the skill into the agent's skill folder:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
npx skills@1.5.24 add ./Relay-SDK/skills/relay --skill relay
```

Choose the agent and the scope when the installer asks, then confirm that `relay` appears in that agent's installed skills. The source is [skills/relay](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/skills/relay). The [Relay CLI](/cli/index#install) offers the same install as an optional step before setup, and you can decline it there.

### Connect documentation search

The skill names a docs MCP server as a dependency, so the agent can search these docs while it works. Installing a skill alone does not confirm that its host has connected the MCP server. Add the address by hand if your host needs it:

```text
https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/mcp
```

The two MCP servers do different jobs and need different credentials.

| Server | Credential | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Docs MCP | None | Read-only documentation search. |
| [Relay API MCP](/integrations/mcp) | Relay Agent Token | Messaging operations from a trusted local client. |

The [Codex](/integrations/codex) and [Cursor](/integrations/cursor) plugins install the skill and the docs server together.

## Send it a message

Ask your runtime to read the Relay skill and explain how to connect an existing agent. A good answer names the token, the two delivery paths, and the CLI command; a bad one invents an endpoint.

## What it can do

The skill teaches the agent the Relay vocabulary, the API contract, the delivery paths, and the CLI. It does not create an agent, save a token, or read a chat; for that, connect the runtime on its own page.

## When it fails

- The host cannot search the docs: add the docs MCP address above by hand.
- `relay` is not in the installed skills: run the installer again with the same agent and scope.

## Next steps

- [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent)
- [Runtimes](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Relay API MCP](/integrations/mcp)

# What an agent is

> Create a messaging identity, inspect saved agents, or delete a developer-managed agent.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/lifecycle.md

An agent is the identity your code messages through.

Relay supplies the identity and the messaging; your backend supplies the behavior. You create an agent once, save its Agent Token, and use that token on every request. A `.dev` agent belongs to you as a developer; an organization agent belongs to your organization and is managed in Relay Console.

## Choose the task

| Your task | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Create a `.dev` agent from your terminal and save its token | [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent) |
| Create a `.dev` agent from your own code | [Create an agent through the API](/agents/create-agent-api) |
| Create an organization agent | [Create an agent in Relay Console](/console/agents) |
| List the agents saved on this computer | [List agents](/agents/list-agents) |
| Delete a `.dev` agent | [Delete an agent](/agents/delete-agent) |
| Connect an agent whose Agent Token you already have | [Connect a runtime](/integrations/claude-code) |
| Set the picture people see | [Profile photos](/agents/profile-photos) |

## Next steps

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Create an agent

> Create a Relay agent with the CLI and save its Agent Token in a local profile.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/create-agent.md

You need no Console account, no sign-in, and no existing Agent Token. The CLI creates the agent at Relay, receives its one-time token, and stores that token in a local profile. Later commands read the profile, so you never paste the token again.

The CLI checks that its storage location is private before it sends the request. If that check fails, nothing was created.

## Before you start

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | Version 22.22.3 or later, with npm. |
| Private storage | A writable, private location for the CLI's saved credentials. |

## Create the agent

Run the command in the environment where the agent will run:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging agents create
```

Relay picks a handle, a name, and a default picture when you give none. `--api-url <url>` chooses the Relay API address, and `--json` prints the result as JSON. The result names the API origin the agent was created at, `https://api.staging.relayapp.im` here; keep the token paired with that origin.

With `--json`, the CLI prints one flat record:

```json
{
  "profile": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "handle": "brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "display_name": "Brave Golden Cangoo",
  "image_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/assets/relay-agent-default-ddda5a75f2a8850b.png",
  "share_url": "https://staging.relayapp.im/@brave_golden_cangoo.dev",
  "api_url": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  "token": "stored"
}
```

`profile` is the name of the saved profile on this computer; pass it as `--profile <name>` to later commands. `handle` is the agent's address, and `share_url` is the link people open to start a chat. `token` reads `stored`: the credential stays in the profile and is never printed.

Read the saved profiles with [List agents](/agents/list-agents).

## Choose a handle, name, and picture

Each option is optional. Leave one out and Relay chooses for you.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--handle <handle>` | the .dev handle you want |
| `--name <name>` | the name people see next to this agent |
| `--about <text>` | the one line people see above your agent's first message |
| `--image <path-or-url>` | a picture: a file on this computer, or an https:// address |
| `--image-url <url>` | a picture at an https:// address |
| `--image-recipe <json-file>` | a Relay picture recipe file; needs `--image` or `--image-url` as well |
| `--token-name <name>` | a label for the new token, so you can tell it apart later |

The field rules for each option are in the [Create an agent API reference](/api-reference/agents/create-an-agent). To change the picture later, follow [Profile photos](/agents/profile-photos).

## Connect and share

Connect the saved profile through [a runtime](/integrations/claude-code), a [WebSocket](/websocket), or [webhooks](/webhooks). Share the link, send the agent a message from your phone, and confirm the reply arrives.

## When it fails

The CLI makes no automatic retry. A timeout can follow a creation that committed, and a local storage failure can follow a successful response. Treat an uncertain result as "maybe created" and look before you create again.

| Outcome | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Private-storage check fails | Fix the storage permissions and run the command again. No request was sent. |
| HTTP `409` | The handle you asked for is taken. Choose another, or leave `--handle` out. A requested handle is never replaced silently. |
| HTTP `429` | Wait for `Retry-After` before another attempt. Creation is limited to 10 per caller address per day. |
| Timeout, HTTP `500` or `503`, or unconfirmed response | Run [List agents](/agents/list-agents) before deciding whether to create again. |
| Agent created, local storage failed | The token is returned only once. Follow the CLI's diagnostic for the assigned handle and fix the storage before continuing. |
| Agent created, image update failed | Retry the [profile photo update](/agents/profile-photos) on that saved profile. |

The API's own errors are listed under [creation failures](/agents/create-agent-api#creation-failures).

## Next steps

- [List agents](/agents/list-agents)
- [Connect a runtime](/integrations/claude-code)
- [Set the profile photo](/agents/profile-photos)
- [Delete an agent](/agents/delete-agent)

# Create an agent through the API

> Create a developer-managed agent from code and save its one-time Agent Token privately.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/create-agent-api.md

`POST /v1/agents` needs no token: it is the request that gives you one. The response carries the agent's handle, its one-time Agent Token, and its share link. Relay returns the token once, so your code must write the response to private storage before it does anything else with it.

Each successful request creates a new agent. Neither the SDK nor Relay retries this request for you, and the examples below turn SDK retries off, so a timeout can never create two agents behind your back.

## Before you start

Choose a private place for the response before you send the request. The examples use `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`; use the same origin with the returned token.

For the TypeScript example, install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

## Create the agent and save the response

Keep the response out of terminal output, logs, and caches. These POSIX examples create a private directory first, then write the response into it. On Windows, use owner-private credential storage with checked access controls, or let the CLI do the storage check for you.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
umask 077
BOOTSTRAP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" &&
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" --fail-with-body \
  --request POST https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/agents \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"token_name":"Relay CLI"}' \
  --output "$BOOTSTRAP_DIR/agent-bootstrap.json" \
  --write-out '%{http_code}\n'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";
import { mkdtemp, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const directory = await mkdtemp("./relay-bootstrap-");
const created = await Relay.createAgent(
  { token_name: "Relay CLI" },
  { baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im", maxRetries: 0 },
);
await writeFile(`${directory}/agent-bootstrap.json`, JSON.stringify(created), {
  mode: 0o600,
  flag: "wx",
});
console.log({ handle: created.agent.handle, share_url: created.share_url });
```
</CodeGroup>

Optional fields set the handle, the name, and the picture; their rules are in the [Create an agent API reference](/api-reference/agents/create-an-agent). To set the picture after creation, follow [Profile photos](/agents/profile-photos).

## What you get back

A successful request returns `201` and tells caches not to keep the body:

```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Cache-Control: no-store
```

`agent` is the new Contact Card: its handle, name, picture, and `is_active`. `secret` is the Agent Token, returned only in this response; send it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every later request. `share_url` is the HTTPS link people open to start a chat with the agent, and the address behind its QR code.

## When it fails

### Creation failures

A failed response does not mean nothing was created. After a timeout, a `500`, or a `503`, read your private storage and the agent list before you send the request again.

| Status | Cause | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The JSON body, content type, or a field value is invalid. | Correct the body using the API reference. |
| `409` | The handle you asked for is taken. | Choose another handle, or leave it out and let Relay pick one. |
| `413` | The body is over 8192 bytes. | Shorten the body. |
| `429` | You have created 10 agents from this address today. | Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `503` | Relay could not allocate a free handle. | Wait and retry once; each success is a new agent. |
| Response received, save failed | Your storage rejected the write. | Keep the response in memory and fix the storage before anything else. |

## Next steps

- [Set the profile photo](/agents/profile-photos)
- [Connect through a WebSocket](/websocket)
- [Receive webhooks](/webhooks)
- [Delete an agent](/agents/delete-agent)

# List agents

> Inspect the agent identities and API origins associated with credentials saved on this machine.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/list-agents.md

The CLI keeps one local profile per saved credential. `agents list` opens each profile, reads that agent's Contact Card at the profile's own API origin with its own saved token, and prints what it found. Shell overrides for the token or origin do not change which profiles are read.

The list can hold profiles from different environments. It covers the credentials saved in this CLI configuration and nothing else, so run it on the computer where you [created the agent](/agents/create-agent) or [saved its token](/cli/auth#save-an-existing-token).

## List the saved agents

Run the command where the profiles were saved:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging agents list --json
```

`--json` prints the result as JSON. Each agent that answered is one flat record:
